findings: No paper label is involved: this is the sharpness of a programme statement (Sbierski 2312.07443's (2.4), Causal/PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy.lean:147 and its M form :191). The findings concern the target's evidence (programme/roadmap.toml, the block of T-abs-meets-cauchy-antisymmetry-sharp), the ladder comment and the library, not ETT.tex.

The target's claim holds as titled, every conjunct, with nothing refuted and no hypothesis added: X ⊆ ℝ² is T2 and second countable; the arc causality (≪ empty) is causally arc-connected and absolutely minimal, plainly and on every open set for every cover; ≤ is not antisymmetric (q ≤ y ≤ q, q ≠ y); {y} is a Cauchy surface (DEC-14); the ray over ℝ is past-inextensible (DEC-13), its point at 0 is q ∈ J⁺({y}), and it misses y (rayCircle_separates_pastInextensible_meets, scaffold :888). Lean ≥ the target: T2 for the theorem's T1, both readings of absolute minimality, and the bare negation over every Hausdorff second countable space (:909).

The evidence's Cauchy argument is correct, with three sharpenings. (a) Its τ, the signed arc length from q, is rayCircleAngle (:407; 1 − x on the ray, the argument on the circle), and its monotonicity off y holds along ≤_U for every open U ∌ y, step by step (:442, :464). (b) The evidence's 'converges to a point of X' needs that a curve missing y stays in one incoming branch. That is true and is proved: the open ray and the open lower half-circle both have τ < 0, are disjoint and open, and τ is monotone, so a connected piece of the curve cannot meet both (:744). (c) The case split 'eventually constant, or converges' is not needed, and 'appending the arc forward from the end' fails as worded for a curve over an interval unbounded above, which has no end to append after. The proof extends every curve missing y along a standard causal curve up to y itself, so the new value is always y, after compressing the parameter by arctan (DEC-11's φ). No limit of the curve is taken, only the supremum of its angle.

What the evidence asked the closer to report as missing: the ETT layer had no extension lemma along a graph without a causality hypothesis. extensible_of_tendsto (Causal/Inextensible.lean:814) asks IsCausal, false here (rayCircle_not_isCausal), and StronglyCausal, which the loop breaks as the evidence says: a small arc about a circle point is not causally convex, since a curve leaves it and comes back round. That last point is argued, not formalised. The end-piece lemmas of Causal.CExtConnexeCauchy.SubArc (pauseTop :116, exists_compress :143, the of_top_tail family :218, :335, :482) handle constant end pieces, not a new piece of a different arc. The model-layer extensible_of_timeGraph_openEnd (Causal/Remarks/SingularRowsCauchyExt.lean:230) is the construction, but it is out of reach (model layer) and asks a time function. New here: Causality.extensible_of_graph (scaffold :260), with no hypothesis on the causality, the space or the interval. From SubArc only CausalCurveIn.comp_monotoneOn (:194) is used.

The arcs are not ArcCoherent (Causal/GHWithoutTarentin.lean:235): the upper half reaches q at parameter 0 and the lower half at 1, and coherence would make the causality causal (ArcCoherent.isCausal, :277). So the one-step tools of GHWithoutTarentin (ArcCoherent.le_iff, :258) do not apply. The monotone angle replaces them: it is the only invariant of ≤_U the proof uses, besides the two inverse formulas Γ(τ(p)) = p on each branch (:708, :733).

The ladder comment above the (2.4) consequences (programme/ladder.toml:5001–5008) says the antisymmetry model was 'argued by the closer, not formalised' and 'Whether each of these is a causality of ETT was not checked in Lean'. For the antisymmetry model both are now settled: it is formalised, and it is an arcCausality absolutely minimal on every open set, so an ETT causality under DEC-167. It is still no [[fails]] entry, because a consequence is not a pair, and no pair moves: causally_arc_connected ∧ absolutely_minimal ⇏ is_causal is already decided by the flat time cylinder.
questions: 'Absolutely minimal on every open set' is read as ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W (for every cover of W, the gluing reading of OQ-18/DEC-167). The plain AbsolutelyMinimal is conjoined too. Both hold, so no reading is chosen.

'≤ is not antisymmetric' is read as ¬ IsCausal, the antisymmetry of ≤ at W = ⊤ (Causal/Properties.lean:95), which is the hcaus of exists_mem_of_mem_Jplus at W = ⊤. The witness q ≤ y ≤ q, q ≠ y is conjoined literally.

'A past-inextensible causal curve along the ray' is read as the evidence suggests: the curve over ℝ that runs inward along the ray for t ≤ 0 and rests at q for t ≥ 0 (rayCircleRay, :836). The form over Iic 0 is not stated separately. Past-inextensibility is DEC-13's, the library's standing reading; 'a point in J⁺(S)' is the point at t = 0.

'{y} is a Cauchy surface of X' is read as DEC-14's IsCauchySurface (every inextensible causal curve meets S in exactly one point), the library's standing reading. y = (−1, 0) as the title has it. The argument works for any y ≠ q on the circle, but only this y is formalised.
kb_proposals: Sbierski's (2.4) needs ≤ antisymmetric: Causal.rayCircle_separates_pastInextensible_meets (CausalScaffold.MeetsCauchyAntisymmetrySharp). The carrier is the unit circle with the ray {(1 + r, 0)} at q = (1, 0), with an arcCausality absolutely minimal on every open set. q ≤ y ≤ q, {y} is Cauchy, and the ray is past-inextensible through q ∈ J⁺({y}) and misses y. The bare form is not_pastInextensible_exists_mem_of_mem_Jplus_bare (T-abs-meets-cauchy-antisymmetry-sharp).

To show a causal curve is extensible with no causality hypothesis (no IsCausal, no StronglyCausal), use Causal.Causality.extensible_of_graph. If c = γ ∘ h on I, with h continuous and non-decreasing, γ a causal curve over J, and γ t' a new value with t' ≥ h(I), then c is extensible over any interval; the parameter is compressed by arctan. It generalises the model-layer extensible_of_timeGraph_openEnd and replaces extensible_of_tendsto for non-causal models (T-abs-meets-cauchy-antisymmetry-sharp).

To show a parametrised path is a causal curve of an arcCausality, use Causal.Causality.causalCurveIn_top_of_pieces. It suffices that γ is continuous and γ s ≤_N γ s' whenever γ maps [s, s'] into the open N, and each such piece is one arcStep along a reparametrised arc (T-abs-meets-cauchy-antisymmetry-sharp).

A Cauchy surface of a non-coherent arc causality, without ArcCoherent: find a function that does not decrease along every arcStep inside the open sets off S (an angle). A connectedness dichotomy between the incoming branches then puts every causal curve missing S on a standard curve at that function, and extensible_of_graph extends it to S. The ray glued to the circle is the model (rayCircle_extensible_of_forall_ne) (T-abs-meets-cauchy-antisymmetry-sharp).
